newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait approves Raytheon $1 bln JV smelter.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait approves Raytheon $1 bln JV smelter.

text.p: Kuwait has approved a plan by Raytheon Co to build a 230,000 tonnes per year (tpy) aluminium smelter worth around $1 billion in a joint venture with local and foreign partners, an official said on Wednesday.
"The finance ministry has approved the business plan proposed by (the U.S. company) Raytheon to build the aluminium project," a finance ministry official said.
"The approval by the (finance) ministry is final but there are other official licences to be acquired," the official said.

The project to build the $1 billion smelter was proposed by Raytheon as a joint venture with local and foreign companies to fulfil an offset obligation incurred on its Gulf War sale to Kuwait of Patriot air-defence missiles and launchers.
"Now that the finance ministry gave the go ahead sign, further steps can be taken," a source close to the project said.
"There are more paper work and preparations before the actual building of the plant," said the source, who asked not to be identified.

Under offset rules introduced after the 1991 Gulf War, foreign firms winning sales contracts worth one million dinars or more have to reinvest 30 percent of a contract's value in a project of their choice after gaining the approval by the government.
Industry sources have said Raytheon has been discussing the technology for the project with U.S. firm Reynolds Metals, which also stood as a potential partner in the project.
